neighbours.label: Unclear, broad: the noun after 'both' that refers back to two alternatives just named (both cases, both types), vs 'each case' and 'both of'
fire: The two towns tried different plans, and in both cases the river still flooded.
Where both kinds of insurance are offered, buyers often pick the cheaper one.
Doctors compared pills and injections and found both types of treatment worked.
Two witnesses spoke, and in both cases their stories matched.
The shop sells new and used bikes, and both types come with a warranty.
Rain and drought hit the farm, and in both years the harvest was poor.
Where both groups of students were present, the debate grew lively.
The company tested two engines, and both models failed the cold test.
quiet: The two towns tried different plans, and in each case the river still flooded.
Where insurance is offered, buyers often pick the cheaper one.
Doctors compared pills and injections and found that they worked.
Two witnesses spoke, and each of them told the same story.
The shop sells new and used bikes, and every bike comes with a warranty.
Rain and drought hit the farm, and the harvest was poor that year.
Where the students were present, the debate grew lively.
The company tested two engines, and neither passed the cold test.

predictions: 'both cases/types/kinds' 0.25-0.45; 'each case', 'both of them' and plain sentences under 0.1. Expect a weak or failed test: broad pole, max only 3.0.
notes: Card: broad (1.3%), max 3.03; peaks ' types' x3, ' cases' x1 after 'both', plus letters and code pieces. Probe: both types of schools 0.440, both cases 0.277; each case 0.085, both of them 0.098, letters b) and c) 0.091, snow 0.079.
